reports.title: Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars — Week 6 Picker History
reports.intro: Week 6 is Houston at Jacksonville in London: Jaguars -2.5, total 42.5. My read is a slight lean to Houston +2.5, but the cleaner position is Houston +8.5 in Raheem’s teaser. The apparent 4–2 Houston consensus is misleading: the actual straight-spread board is tied 2–2.

rows.speaker: Anthony Dabbundo
rows.interpretation: Best overall record. However, he was 3–0 backing Jacksonville and is now reversing course. He is 1–1 backing Houston and 1–0 fading them.

rows.speaker: Joe House
rows.interpretation: Major warning: 1–4 backing Houston, including losses on his two previous Houston Wise Wagers. His Week 5 Houston teaser won, but this is a much more aggressive straight bet.

rows.speaker: Raheem Palmer
rows.interpretation: His structure is historically intelligent: he avoids the straight line and lowers conviction. He is 1–2 backing Houston but 3–1 backing Jacksonville in graded bets.

rows.speaker: Craig Trapp
rows.interpretation: Small sample, but he is 2–0 laying favorite prices involving these teams and previously won with Jacksonville -8.5.

rows.speaker: Simon Hunter
rows.interpretation: He is 1–0 backing Jacksonville, but 0–2 fading them. Conversely, he is 0–2 backing Houston and 1–0 fading Houston. His current side fits his better team-specific split.

rows.speaker: Chad Millman
rows.interpretation: Weakest historical support for Houston: 0–4 backing the Texans. His refusal to take +2.5 is important—the key number, not Houston itself, is the appeal.

reports.favorite_records: Favorite/underdog records: Dabbundo is 2–0 on favorite contracts and 3–1 on underdogs; House is 3–4 on favorites and 1–1 on underdogs; Raheem is 3–2 on favorites and 1–1 on graded underdogs; Craig is 2–0 on graded favorites; Simon is 1–2 on favorites and 1–2 on underdogs; Chad is 1–3 on favorites and 0–2 on underdogs.
notable: Dabbundo is the strongest individual handicapper in this subset, but this pick requires him to fade a Jacksonville team he previously backed successfully three times.
House’s confidence should not be mistaken for historical reliability. He explicitly acknowledged that his first two Houston Wise Wagers lost.
Raheem’s teaser is the best match between current bet and historical performance: his standard-confidence positions are 4–0, while his high-confidence positions are 0–3.

The Jacksonville support is quieter but cleaner: both Craig and Simon are making ordinary straight bets, while two of the four nominal Houston supporters require substantial protection—Raheem at +8.5 and Chad only at +3.
Among speakers without a current selection, Danny went 4–0 backing Jacksonville or fading Houston in Weeks 3–4, while Cousin Sal went 3–1 and was much better fading Houston than backing it.
reports.expectation: Expectation: Houston’s defense should keep this inside one possession, but Jacksonville’s London advantage and Houston’s repeated late-game failures make the moneyline less attractive. Texans +8.5 teaser is the strongest construction; Texans +2.5 is a smaller lean; I would not follow Dabbundo onto the moneyline.

rows.interpretation: His only prior graded contract involving these teams was Titans moneyline in Week 3, a loss. He is 0-1 backing Tennessee and has no prior Colts sample.

rows.speaker: Cousin Sal
rows.interpretation: He is 1-0 backing Indianapolis but 0-2 backing Tennessee. His favorite contracts are 2-1, so the reduced-risk Colts structure fits better than a full spread.

rows.speaker: Chad Millman
rows.interpretation: He is 2-1 backing Indianapolis and 1-1 fading Tennessee. This is the most aggressive Colts position, but both his high-confidence and favorite-contract records are 2-1.

rows.speaker: Simon Hunter
rows.interpretation: Strongest history here: 2-0 backing Indianapolis, 2-0 fading Tennessee, and 3-0 on favorite contracts. The moneyline removes the only real concern—the full 6.5-point margin.

reports.favorite_records: Favorite/underdog records: Craig is 0-0 on favorites and 0-1 on underdogs; Sal is 2-1 on favorites and 1-3 on underdogs; Chad is 2-1 on favorites and 1-1 on underdogs; Simon is 3-0 on favorites and 2-1 on underdogs.
notable: Simon has the cleanest alignment between history and current position: he has won both prior Colts bets, both prior Titans fades, both standard-confidence decisions, and all three favorite contracts.

Sal's history argues for the teaser rather than Colts -6.5: he is only 3-4 overall in this subset, but 1-0 backing Indianapolis and 2-1 on favorite contracts.

reports.expectation: Expectation: Indianapolis is the better-supported side, but the historical evidence favors winning the game more than clearing 6.5. Simon’s Colts moneyline/survivor position is the best construction, Sal’s -0.5 teaser is next, and Chad’s -6.5 is a smaller play. Craig’s Titans +6.5 is the value counterposition, not the history-backed one.

reports.title: Jets at Patriots — Week 6 Picker History
reports.intro: Current board: Indian Cowboy has Jets +6.5; Joe House has Jets +7.5; Anthony Dabbundo and Cousin Sal use Patriots -1.5 teaser legs; Chad Millman has Patriots -7.5 lean; Simon Hunter's final position is Patriots -7 standard. The nominal count is Patriots 4-2, but the true straight-spread board is 2-2 and House owns the key +7.5.

rows.speaker: Indian Cowboy
rows.interpretation: He is 1-1 backing the Jets and 0-1 fading New England, while going 3-1 backing the Patriots. This repeats his Week 5 Jets backing but also repeats his failed Week 5 Patriots fade.

rows.speaker: Joe House
rows.interpretation: He is 2-3 backing the Jets, but 1-0 fading New England. He flips from a winning Week 5 Patriots -3.5 bet; the extra half-point above 7 is the main attraction.

rows.speaker: Anthony Dabbundo
rows.interpretation: He is 1-0 backing the Jets but 1-2 fading New England and has no prior graded Patriots backing. The teaser acknowledges that the full spread is not supported by his history.

rows.speaker: Cousin Sal
rows.interpretation: He is 1-0 backing New England and won Patriots -3.5 last week. He also won Jets -1.5 last week, so the current teaser is a controlled flip rather than a strong anti-Jets trend.

rows.speaker: Chad Millman
rows.interpretation: He is 1-0 backing the Jets and 1-0 fading New England, then reverses both patterns here. His only support is structural: he is 1-1 on favorite contracts versus 1-0 on an underdog teaser.

rows.speaker: Simon Hunter
rows.interpretation: Weakest overall history: 1-2 backing the Jets, 0-1 fading them, and 2-3 fading New England with no prior Patriots backing. The positive is that he is 3-2 on favorites but 0-4 on underdogs.

reports.favorite_records: Favorite/underdog records: Indian Cowboy is 2-1 on favorites and 2-3 on underdogs; House is 2-0 on favorites and 2-3 on underdogs; Dabbundo is 1-1 on favorites and 1-1 on underdogs; Sal is 3-3 on favorites with no graded underdog contract; Chad is 1-1 on favorites and 1-0 on an underdog teaser; Simon is 3-2 on favorites and 0-4 on underdogs.
notable: The 4-2 Patriots headcount overstates agreement. Dabbundo and Sal only need New England to clear -1.5 in teasers; Chad and Simon are the only speakers laying the actual touchdown-sized spread.
House has the best straight number at Jets +7.5. His Jets history is only 2-3, but the hook above 7 materially improves this ticket compared with Indian Cowboy's +6.5.
Sal has the best current Patriots continuity: he won Patriots -3.5 in Week 5 and now lowers the requirement to -1.5. Dabbundo also flips to New England after losing a Raiders +3.5 Patriots fade.

Chad and Simon's full-spread support is not backed by team-specific success. Chad reverses two successful historical patterns; Simon is 3-6 overall and has never graded a Patriots backing in this set.
Indian Cowboy repeats two Week 5 ideas at once—backing the Jets and fading New England—but only the Jets leg worked last week.
reports.expectation: Expectation: do not treat this as a four-person Patriots consensus. The best straight-spread construction is House’s Jets +7.5 because it captures the key-number hook. If using a valid teaser, Patriots -1.5 through Sal is the cleaner New England position. Laying -7 or -7.5 requires more confidence than the historical records justify.
